name: Committed to Wrong Branch
problem: You made several commits, only to realize you were on the `main` branch instead of your feature branch. You haven't pushed yet.

steps.title: Create the branch you meant to be on
steps.description: First, create a new branch from your current state. This safely saves your commits to the correct branch name.
steps.code:
git branch feature-new-ui

# NOTE: Just branch, don't checkout yet.

steps.title: Reset the main branch back
steps.description: Now you need to remove those commits from the main branch. Assuming you made 3 accidental commits, you reset main back by 3.
steps.code:
git reset --hard HEAD~3

# Using --hard makes your working directory match the old state.

steps.title: Switch to your new branch
steps.description: Your commits are safe on the new branch, and main is restored. Switch to the feature branch to continue working.

alternatives.title: Using cherry-pick instead
alternatives.description: If you made the commits on the wrong branch AND pushed them, or if there are other commits mixed in.
alternatives.code:
# 1. Switch to the correct branch
git checkout feature-branch

# 2. Cherry-pick the specific accidental commits
git cherry-pick a1b2c3d e4f5g6h

# 3. Go back to the wrong branch and revert them
git checkout main
git revert a1b2c3d
git revert e4f5g6h
